extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO, OED staff, and parties interested in USPTO disciplinary standards
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing disciplinary findings, sanctions, and post‑order procedures for attorneys and agents registered to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to inform clients about significant Office correspondence (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office by not informing clients about correspondence Respondent received from the Office when the correspondence (i) had a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, (ii) was received by Respondent on behalf [of] clients, and (iii) was correspondence of which a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances the client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion focuses on a practitioner's duty to notify clients of Office correspondence meeting all three listed conditions. Failure to notify in such circumstances constitutes conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice. Apply when correspondence could significantly affect a pending matter, was received on the client's behalf, and a reasonable practitioner would deem client notification appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of legal matters / inadequate client communication (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglecting legal matters entrusted to the practitioner by not adequately communicating with clients about their patent applications, by allowing patent applications to become abandoned without the consent of the respective clients, and by failing to take action to revive abandoned applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether the practitioner maintained adequate communication and took reasonable steps to preserve clients' patent rights (including avoiding abandonment without consent and attempting revival). Examples of misconduct include permitting abandonment without client consent and failing to seek revival where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from practice (term imposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non‑patent law before the Office for a period of twenty‑four (24) months commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctioning criterion: a 24‑month suspension is the concrete disciplinary measure imposed for the violations found in this matter. Use as an example of the Office's sanctioning range for combined failures described above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to conclude client work (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition for a period of thirty (30) days commencing on the date the Final Order is signed for the sole purpose of complying with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c) pertaining to concluding client work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary, narrowly‑tailored authorization to conclude existing client matters only; intended to allow orderly transfer or conclusion of client files consistent with rules governing withdrawal and client protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirty‑one (31) days after the date of the Final Order, the USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and Public Key Infrastructure ('PKI') certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative security/identity step following suspension to prevent further filing or representation using the practitioner's electronic credentials; timing specified as 31 days after Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or obtaining a USPTO Customer Number while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may not apply for, or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that suspended practitioners are barred from obtaining customer numbers enabling electronic practice until formal reinstatement occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation upon reinstatement (24 months) and conditions for enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent successfully petitions for reinstatement in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, Respondent shall be placed on a twenty‑four (24) month probationary period commencing on the date Respondent is reinstated to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation is imposed upon reinstatement; noncompliance during probation can trigger an Order to Show Cause and potential immediate additional suspension. Probation serves as a supervisory and conditional period after reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for probationary violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation, the OED Director shall: (A) issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not enter an order immediately suspending Respondent for up to an additional twenty‑four (24) months; (B) send the Order to Show Cause to Respondent at the last address of record furnished pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a); and (C) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies procedural protections and timeline: issuance, service to last address on record, and a 15‑day response window before further action is taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to USPTO Director and possible immediate additional suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after the 15‑day response period and consideration of any response, the OED Director continues to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director: (i) the Order to Show Cause, (ii) Respondent's response, if any, and (iii) argument and evidence supporting the OED Director's opinion, and request that the USPTO Director enter an order immediately suspending Respondent for up to an additional twenty‑four (24) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes escalation: the OED Director may seek immediate additional suspension by forwarding the record and request to the USPTO Director; this is the enforcement mechanism for probationary or post‑order violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of additional suspension (administrative effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended pursuant to the preceding subparagraph: (1) the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; and (2) Respondent may not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterates administrative effects that follow an additional suspension and maintains prohibition on electronic credentials and customer numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of review on immediate suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that the USPTO Director enters an order immediately suspending Respondent for up to an additional twenty‑four (24) months, and Respondent seeks a review of the USPTO Director's action, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the USPTO Director's order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that seeking review does not stay an immediately‑entered suspension; suspension remains effective during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice requirements (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room electronically located at: http://des.uspto.gov/FoialOEDReadingRoom.jsp; and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Suspension' wording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires public dissemination of the disciplinary Final Order via the OED Reading Room and Official Gazette and prescribes the substance/format of the public notice (including registration number, summary of violations, suspension/probation terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates cross‑jurisdictional notification so that other disciplinary authorities and courts are informed of USPTO discipline and its grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings (aggravating/rebuttal use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Proposed Settlement Agreement or this Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct brought to the attention of the Office, and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding (i) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that prior discipline may be used as aggravation or rebuttal in future matters; practitioners should expect prior records to factor into subsequent disciplinary assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that each party is responsible for its own costs in this settlement—useful precedent for cost allocation in negotiated disciplinary settlements.
